question.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the following double-angle formula for cosine: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2x=1-2{sin}^{2}⁡x
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the following double-angle formula for the hyperbolic cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x=1+2{sinh}^{2}⁡x
$$

We can rearrange the above formula as

$$
2{sinh}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x-1.
$$

We can now integrate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(6+6{sinh}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =3{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(2+2{sinh}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(2+\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x+x)\,{|}_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\  & =3(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sinh}⁡(2\operatorname{ln}⁡2)+\operatorname{ln}⁡2) \\  & =3(\frac{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-{e}^{-2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}}{4}+\operatorname{ln}⁡2) \\  & =3(\frac{{2}^{2}-{2}^{-2}}{4}+\operatorname{ln}⁡2) \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡2+\frac{45}{16}\end{aligned}
$$
